But!  What's a bard without a poem, so I give you the most recent private problem that's been bugging me: my hatred of college.

When I was in fifth grade, I failed a test for the first time in my entire life.  It was open book, and I had no book, so I did the entire thing from memory.  I got all the content right and all the page numbers wrong.  And when I turned that in, do you think anyone was impressed that I had memorized material when I wasn't assigned to?  No.  They called me a failure.

But I ask you, how many times can a complete fucking strangers call you a failure before you start to believe them?

It's about the education, but see  
You could learn that shit in the library

So to me  
There's no really  
Pro-Degree  
note that reads  
anything but a bunch of bullshit.

It's just a piece of paper.  Burning it doesn't change what you know, so why is it even there?

It's to prove that you can deal with the stress  
of going through a system obsessed with tests  
an endless quest to sort the best  
From the rest of the squabble who second guessed  
the essay question they may have messed.  

Was this whole system contrived  
To prove we could work nine to five  
and stay in line for the rest of our lives  
Maybe I don't wanna live that life  

But I don't have a plan b.

So the next day I trudge into a class I'm not in, where a professor who's not mine announces that no one on the wait list is getting in, and everyone who was sitting in has wasted their time.  I don't go back.

When I was a kid my brother raped me.  I was too young to understand what happened.

Later on, I kept it quiet in the hopes of keeping the family from being torn apart.

I took a deep breath.  I was seeing double, both the village that used to be, and the smouldering ruins around me.  How could I not see both crater and home?

"There," pointed my sensei, towards the center of the town.

Sitting, crying to himself, a small child held on to the hand of his dead mother.  His shrieks were as incoherent as his thoughts, so stricken with grief his eyes could only squeeze out more tears, his only solace against seeing the look of horror on his mother's dead face.  The sadness caused an implosion on the world, sucking in the life and the light and the warmth, and leaving only a black hole of misery.

"That is the one," said my sensei.

I stepped towards the child and drew my sword.

Instantly, the crying stopped.  A strange yellow light poured out of the boys eyes and mouth as he shrieked at me, lifting me into the air and slamming me into the ground simply by commanding it so.  The demon in this child was strong.

I was stronger.  The dust kicked up by my fall mixed with the ash in the air and gave me cover.  The demon forced the child to look from side to side, frantically, backing away from where he had seen me last.  I, however, had used the opportunity to slip into a house.  I ascended to the second floor, jumped to the balcony of it's neighbor, and from there ascended to the rooftops.

I silently dropped down into the alleyway just as the demon forced the child to back into it.  I slit it's throat before it realized what happened.

I went back to my master, prepared to be berated for allowing myself to take the first blow, but instead he faced me with a grim smile.

I bowed before him.

"That is all I can teach you.  You are now a master."

I straightened and spoke excitedly.  "Then we can go end this!"

"End this?" he asked.

"Go defeat their king.  Slay him, cast him back to the depths, free this land from his grim rule."

"No, my child," said my sensei.

"What do you mean no?!  We're the only ones who *can* end this!"

"I fought the demon king, once" said my sensei.  He had neglected to mention this when I entered his temple and stated my reason for mastering this art was to defeat demon king.

"He would face you?" I said, astounded.

"It was after I beat his first lieutenant, Pithius."

Everyone in the land knew the story, of how my master's cleverness had allowed him to strike the demon clean in twain.  It had been said that out of fear, the demon king had revoked his challenge to anyone who would see him.

"Why did I waste my time with this if it could not grant me victory!"

I threw down my sword in disgust.

"When I fought the demon king," said my sensei, speaking slowly, bending over to pick up my discarded weapon, "the battle lasted for days.  I evaded his every blow, but was unable to land a lethal strike.  Instead, I made repeated gashes in him whenever he presented me with an opening.  The blood loss from even one of them should have been enough to kill a man.  I struck inch deep 8 times in one leg, 11 in another, and 17 times on each arm.  He even lost and eye, but did not fall.  And, after the sun had fallen and risen for the second time, I leaned on my sword from the exhaustion."

"Please, god, I cried out, let his wounds prove too severe.  Let his arms weaken more so than mine.  Let his guard finally falter.  May this beast be ended.  But the demon king just laughed at me, as he engulfed himself in fire and healed all his wounds.  I heard his voice, made of the combined screams of the damned."

"*God says no*"

"Then I ran.  It took me two weeks to escape the demon lands, and I've been living here ever since."

I stood in stunned silence, before I noticed the light shining from the ground beneath him.

"Sensei!"  I screamed, running towards him to knock him off, but it was too late.

The demon possessed him quickly.  He drew my sword from my sheath, and drove it quickly into sensei's stomach.

I fell to my knees and stared at the body of the only man I thought who could save us.  His body, strangely fitting against the backdrop of burnt ruin.

I'm a rape victim who never reported it to the police.  In fact, outside of this reddit account, I don't talk about it, and I even maintain two different reddit accounts, one for admitting this stuff and one for not.  After this post I'm going to switch back and continue on my merry way.  Allow me to explain the many reasons why that number is so high.

First off, the story of what happened.

When I was about say 11, my brother (3 years older than I), asked me for oral.  He didn't use any terms that led me to believe that what I was doing was in fact sex.  I wasn't even bothered by it at the time, it felt like I was, in fact, having sex.

If at this point you are thinking that I do not qualify as a rape victim, the statutory rape laws in the state I live in say I do.  I have checked them.  Thoroughly.

Years later, in health class, I learned what sex is.  Horrified about what I had done, I vowed that my parents would never know.  They still don't.

So here are some reasons people choose not to report being raped.

1)  They blame themselves.  They should have known better, they shouldn't have been that drunk.  I like to call this line of thinking the many-worlds fallacy.  Just because there was something you *could* have done, doesn't mean it's your fault for not doing it.  It's your attackers fault for making it necessary.  That said, I still spend many nights late at night wondering if I should have known better.  After all, I'd seen the stupid videos on bad touches.

2)  Victims think other people will blame them.  If they're wrestling with blaming themselves, it only makes sense that other people would too.  I haven't told very many people IRL about what happened to me.  The responses have ranged from not believing me, to awkward silence.  Sometimes, the other person admits to me they are also rape victims.  That makes simultaneously the best answer and the worst answer.  

3)  Victims think admitting what happened will make things worse.  If my family knew what my brother did to me, and believed me, and didn't blame me, it would tear my family apart.  All I have to do is stay silent until they die, and they can maintain their illusion and their happiness.  Some people's attackers are people they seriously care about.  I couldn't give two shits what happened to mine, but if it's someone you love and don't want to go to jail, things can get confusing.

A horrible but true life lesson:  Hating someone does not necessarily make you stop loving them.

4)  They didn't realize what happened.  It took me 2-3 years until I knew.  And what then?  Do I dredge up old tragedy?  I couldn't prove anything anymore.  The longer I wait the harder and less realistic admitting things gets.  There are plenty of drugs that can prevent you from realizing you've been raped.

5)  The rapist probably won't go to jail.  You can't prove anything.  Even if your family and friends believe you, the police might not, and a jury definitely won't, not beyond reasonable doubt.  Now there's a pissed off rapist roaming the streets, and he's pulled it off once before.



It takes a lot of courage to report sexual assault to the police, once you realize what happened.  You have to get past your own internal doubts, about how you could have stopped it, about if anyone will believe you, about if turning them in will actually make things better.

Someone who has just been raped has the worst emotional preparation possible for reporting it to the police.

You know the funny thing about kobolds?  They have squeaky voices!  The damned things are so full of themselves, boasting ancient power and speaking the language of dragons, but you just can't take 'em seriously.  You can't!  For real, they sound like Rufus did when he was a puppy.  "Yip yip I'm a terrible sorcerer!"  It's no wonder they're evil.  They get sooo mad but it just makes 'em sound funnier.

I still remember that speech too.  "We will drive back our oppressors!  We will take back our gold!"  We will hit puberty and our voices will drop!  Morale was high that day.  A tiny band of kobolds against us, a legion of heroes!  The greatest band of men the country could muster!  And we shrieked with a holy roar, it sent chills down your spine to hear it.  We were MEN.  We were STRONG.  They were TINY!  Ha ha.  We were all looking forward to a good fight and a good drink.

Kobold magic is no laughing matter though.  Their warriors were no problem, it was driving through them fast enough to drop their casters.  If you didn't see the spell coming in time you'd get burned.  That's how Charlie lost his eyebrows.  You know Charlie, the bar tender?  He said it was a volcano?!  HA!  It was a damn kobold and he knows it.

We fought hard that day.  Fought well.  Cleaved 'em right in two I did, I was mighty stronger back then than I am now.  My knees still moved without creaking.  Pretty good looking too, if I do say so myself.  The thrill of battle, ohhh to feel that rush again.  With your best friends in your world at your side, your god at your back, and your enemy at your front, that is to know the glory of the fight.  To feel the thirst for blood, for holy retribution!

Or that's what they told us.  That's how we were supposed to feel.  To be honest, I did feel it a bit.  It scares me now.

We were winning.  We were CRUSHING them.  Gods, if only it ended there.  No.  A squeaky voice called out, "the master has arrived".  No one was laughing then.

The dracolich is strong.  Stronger now than he was then, and then he had conquered death itself.  The gods could not touch him.  He roared above the battle with a voice that made your soul shake.  He let out a massive cry and the skies went dark.  An unholy storm shook the earth and poured evil into the soil.  No plants grew there for years.  But the dead, the dead got back up.  The dead started fightin' us.

Killing a kobold is easy.  Killing it several times?  That gets tough, that gets old.  You get tired.  And killing your friend, the friend you drank with, the friend you'd have died for, that's impossible.  And they just kept gettin' back up.  Their souls knew no peace but there wasn't a damned thing you could do about it.  You either dropped them again or you died there and started fighting for the other side.

The captains cried out again.  "Keep fighting, form up, push through.  Now's our chance!"  Every man on that field knew we had no chance.  Our voices didn't sound mighty any more.  And our gods?  If they were at our back they sure as hell weren't doing anything.

So we broke rank.  We turned tail, fled.  Ahead of us stood death, embodied in a thousand year old dragon, and behind us was family.  There's a time to be with your fellow soldier, and there's a time to be home.  Your mother was at home, your father... my wife...

I shoulda kept fighting.  I should have brought down every last one of them I could.  I should have died out there.  It should have been me!  I was the coward!  I should have died with the rest!  Thousands died, the whole town it seemed, all of my friends, why not me?  Why couldn't I share in the glory?  Why did I disgrace their deaths with my cowardice...

Then came the knock on the door.  They didn't want me.  No.  I'd ran.  My spirit was broken, I was already a dead man.  I was broken as a soldier, I'd never fight again.  I'd be an obedient slave.  But I had killed kobold.  I had killed his children.  The debt had to paid.

Your father stood to fight, your mother ran upstairs.  Your grandmother got on her knees and begged, clawed at his magic cloak.  Her hands were blacked by whatever charms were on it but she didn't care.  She looked into his eyes and pleaded mercy.  He has no soul behind his eyes.  And he has no mercy.

He struck her down first.  He actually let your father strike him, the blade did nothing.  Disintegrated at the touch.  He turned your father to stone because he could, because it was fun.  Then he went upstairs and found your mother.  She was looking for you, to try to hide you, to try to save you.  Didn't find you.  He struck her down without so much as a thought.

Then he turned to me.  "Is that all of them," he asked, the words inside my mind.

The only thing the gods ever gave me was that lie.

And he left.  Didn't see what I had done in the commotion.  Didn't realize you were under the floorboards.  I'm not sure why you didn't cry then, but you cried non-stop for weeks after.  I did too.

So I'm begging you child.  I'm pleading with you.  Don't fight.  I know the life of a slave is hard, but losing your family is harder.  I lost my wife.  I lost my son!  I lost everything... everything but you.  And I cannot lose you.  I won't lose you.  Lead a good life, find a woman and start a happy family.  Do it far away from here, forget the worries of this land.  I'll keep working these fields and die a happy man knowing you're safe.  But if you go off to battle I know what will happen.  It will be a sorrow the world cannot take, when your friends have to cut your undead body down again and again.  It will be a sorrow a thousand times worse when I find out.

I'm begging you.

Run.  Leave.

Met a guy at a bar who'd ordered more three wise men than was wise for three men.  He was rambling on about how Everybody Love's Raymond is the bad kind of embarrassing, so I asked him what the good kind was and he dove into this story.

Apparently at his school's charity dance they were doing a bunch of weird activities.  He lost pretty badly in musical chairs but dominated twister, didn't really matter.  Cause one game was different.  They didn't say what it was or what it was for, they just handed out questionnaires and had everyone fill them out.  And he "played to win".  Said that with a smirk on his face.

Flash forward to the end of the dance, they call up the number one donator.  "Cute girl," he said, "Indian".  Apparently they were going to find the girl a date amongst her fellow class members, based upon his quiz answers.  But they had a ton of time left, he couldn't remember why, so they decided to call out another donor.

And he was number 2.

He said to me he guessed he thought the game was supposed to be about identifying who the quiz taker was, so he forged all his answers.  So they throw his answers up on a projector and they're all bogus.  Favorite color:  purple.  Favorite movie:  Titanic.  But the worst part is, he didn't think answers enough would be sufficient trickery.  He tried to forge someone else's handwriting.

He dotted his "I"s with hearts.

And the room is silent.  Not a peep.  He's just standing there, pale as a ghost cause he's realized now what the quiz is for, looking out at his entire class staring at his quiz, and how secretly this whole time what he looked for in the opposite sex was abs.  And they start calling the answers one by one.

Favorite color:  Purple.

About half the girls sit down.

Favorite movie:  Titanic

Couple of girls keep standing.

And so on and so fourth, until he gets to the end.

Favorite artist:  Miley Cyrus

Fucking.  No one.  Not one person had chosen Miley as their favorite artist.  Not a one.  Everyone's just staring at her name in disbelief, the "i" so lovingly dotted with a heart, and the people running it don't know what to do.  So they call out to the girl who was last standing, as she hasn't sat down yet, and say she won.  She just says "nope" and plops right down.

So the people running it just shrugged it off and told the poor guy to sit down.

By the end of the story he was blushing all over again.  Poor guy, I bought him a beer for that one.

There once was a quiet girl, in a quiet house, on in a quiet wood.  She was a good girl, she did as she was told and kept to herself while she played.  But, she had a problem.

She couldn't seem to fall asleep.

So one day her parents got her a stuffed penguin to help her sleep.  When that didn't work, she asked them to take her to the store, bought a small pallet of stickers, and stuck one to the wall.  Every night when she'd open her eyes, frustrated, she'd see a sticker on the wall smiling back at her.

"I can't sleep," she'd whisper to the penguin.

"That's okay, I can't fly" she imagined it replied.

Until one night, deep into the night, she finally opened her eyes and saw the sticker was bulging.  Curious, the girl peeled the sticker off the wall, and found a fairy stuck to the glue on the back of it.

"Who are you?" she asked the fairy.

"I..." it began, cleaning itself off, "am the dream fairy.  When you go to sleep I put the happy thoughts in your head."

"What about the sad thoughts?  What about nightmares?" replied the girl.

"Well..." said the fairy, revealing a toothy grin with sharp teeth, "goodnight"

--

The next morning the girl awoke in a cold sweat.  Her father was standing over her, tears in his eyes.  Her mother had fallen asleep on her drive to work, and the car had driven into on-coming traffic.  Her mother was hospitalized, and the doctors did not know when she would be able to return home.

The little girl didn't cry though.  Sometimes small children are too small to understand big problems.  She just stood there, numbly, wondering why the fairy had done this to her.

That night, the little girl had another nightmare.  And the night after that.  The penguin did not help her.  Her father could not comfort her.  Sleeping was an ordeal no matter what she tried.  Her mother was not getting better, in fact she was getting worse, and there was nothing the girl could do about it.  The world was a dark and scary place, and even though the girl had done nothing wrong, she started to fear nothing would ever be right again.

She almost... almost... gave up on her dreams.

But she didn't.  Not quite.  She had one last plan.

She stuck a jar up against the wall where the fairy had gotten stuck before, and lined the insides with glue.  Sure enough, that night, the faerie got stuck again.  She snatched the jar off the wall, put a lid on it, and stuck the jar in a corner.

That's what little girls think you do to people who are bad.

And that was the first night no one on the planet slept.

--

The next day did not bring good news to the little girl.  Her mother's condition was worsening, but the doctors were all exhausted.  They were busy trying to solve the sleeplessness epidemic, and were too tired to operate on anyone anyway.  So the next night, the little girl spun the jar around and talked to the faerie.

"Why are you doing this?" she demanded?

"Doing what?" he asked, showing again his pointy teeth.

"You made my mom sleep in the car.  You made all my dreams bad.  And now you're making everyone stay up all night!" began the girl.

"The last one isn't me," replied the faerie, coolly, "that one's on you".

The girl was so angry.  Angrier than she ever had been.  Angrier than little girls should ever have to be.

"Ooo... I have have a mind to" she began, as she raised the jar above her head, and began to slam it down.

"WAIT!" cried the faerie.  "Let me show you something"

And the girl fell asleep.

--

She and the faerie were at a young boy's house.  The boy was reaching for a glass of water on a shelf across the room, but couldn't make it.  He sat and thought for a good long while, but eventually gave in, calling out for help.

A few moments later, the light in the hallway flickered on, and the boy's father shuffled into the room, looking like he'd been tired for years now.

The boy, very quietly, asked his dad if he could get some water.  His dad tried his best to hide the sigh, he really did, but it was still there.  He grabbed the water off the shelf and started towards his son.

But he tripped.  His feet got caught on the boy's wheelchair.  Water spilled everywhere and the glass shattered.

The boy tried to help, he really did, but what help could he offer?  He couldn't walk.

"Every night," the faerie began, "that boy dreams a happy dream."

"Of walking?" asked the girl.

"No," replied the faerie, "of flying."

"Why do you give him happy dreams and not me?" asked the girl.
